comparisons.peer_topic: Embedded segment net revenue and drivers for fiscal year 2024
comparisons.peer_summary: Embedded net revenue decreased by 33% to $3.6 billion in 2024 from $5.3 billion in 2023, primarily due to lower demand as customers normalized inventory levels.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD attribute fiscal 2024 revenue performance directly to the normalization of channel inventory levels following prior periods of destocking. NVDA reports that Graphics revenue increased 15% in Gaming driven by 'higher sell-in to partners following the normalization of channel inventory levels.' Similarly, AMD reports that its Embedded segment net revenue decreased 33% primarily because 'customers continued to normalize their inventory levels,' indicating that while NVDA’s segment benefited from restocking (higher sell-in), AMD’s segment was still impacted by the ongoing or recent phase of inventory normalization affecting demand.

sentences.text: Graphics revenue - The year-on-year increase was led by growth in Gaming of 15% driven by higher sell-in to partners following the normalization of channel inventory levels.
The decrease in net revenue was primarily due to lower demand as customers continued to normalize their inventory levels.

comparisons.comparison: While NVDA attributes its 2024 revenue growth to operational factors like channel inventory normalization and product demand, Broadcom attributes its significant 2024 expense growth primarily to acquisition-related headcount and compensation changes from the VMware merger. NVDA’s financial driver is sales volume ('higher sell-in'), whereas AVGO’s driver is cost structure expansion ('higher compensation... from the VMware Merger'). This highlights a divergence in business drivers: NVDA is experiencing organic demand recovery, while AVGO is facing integration-related cost increases.

comparisons.peer_summary: DCAI revenue increased 1% from 2023, driven by higher server revenue from high core count products, which increased average selling prices but lowered volume compared to 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and INTC discuss drivers for their respective server/data center revenue segments in fiscal 2024, but with contrasting outcomes and causes. NVDA’s Graphics segment saw strong growth (15%) driven by channel normalization. In contrast, Intel’s Data Center and AI (DCAI) segment saw only flat revenue growth (1% increase), driven by a mix shift toward higher-average selling price (ASR) high core count products which resulted in lower volume. NVDA benefited from volume/sell-in increases, while INTC’s revenue was sustained by ASP increases despite volume declines.

comparisons.peer_topic: QCT segment revenue drivers and EBT margin change
comparisons.peer_summary: QCT revenues in fiscal 2024 increased primarily due to higher handset revenues driven by $2.8 billion in higher chipset shipments from major OEMs and higher automotive revenues from new vehicle launches with Snapdragon products, partially offset by lower IoT revenues; QCT EBT as a percentage of revenues increased primarily due to these higher revenues.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and QCOM explicitly cite the normalization of channel inventory levels as a key driver for their respective segment revenue growth in fiscal 2024. NVDA states its Gaming revenue increase was 'driven by higher sell-in to partners following the normalization of channel inventory levels.' QCOM states its QCT revenue increase was primarily due to higher handset revenues driven by 'normalization of customer inventory levels, which were elevated in the prior year.' Both companies demonstrate a similar recovery pattern where previous inventory drawdowns normalized, leading to increased downstream sell-in and revenue growth.
